chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Abu al-Khattab, from Wahb ibn Hafsh, from Abu Basir, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who emancipated his slave while he had a debt, fleeing from the debt. He said: 'There is no emancipation for him (if done to flee debt), and if he emancipated him while in good health and soundness, there is no claim of the creditor upon him (the slave).'

key_terms.دَبَّرَ: Emancipated (specifically tadbir, a form of partial or conditional manumission)
key_terms.فِرَاراً مِنَ الدَّيْنِ: Fleeing from the debt (purpose of emancipation)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a master emancipating his slave to avoid paying off his debts?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the validity of *tadbir* (emancipation upon death) when a master incurs debt specifically to evade creditors. The ruling distinguishes that if the emancipation was a genuine act during health and solvency, creditors cannot claim the slave, but if it was a strategic move to avoid debt, the *tadbir* is considered invalid. This highlights the Shia juristic principle of examining the master's intent and financial state at the time of the act to determine the rights of creditors versus the slave's freedom.
